identity.name: BAJAJ HEALTHCARE LIMITED
identity.industry: Pharmaceuticals — API & FDF (Finished Dosage) manufacturer for global generics; moving up to Peptides / Oncology / specialty CDMO

summary.oneLiner: First-ever concall frames a two-vertical story — a stable, deleveraging API base (rev +11.3% YoY, GM 48.3% +210 bps, D/E down to 0.45) funding a move up the value chain into Peptides (250 kg/yr plant, first product Semaglutide, commissioning Q4 FY27), Oncology API (Q4 2028), specialty CNS formulations (Cenobamate — first-in-India SEC nod) and backward integration (China dependency reduction, incl. a fermentation-route Vitamin C with ICT by 2029). Modest near-term guide (10-15% rev, 18-20% EBITDA) with a Rs.900-1,000 cr revenue aspiration in 2-3 years riding the new plants.

financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Rs.165.6 cr | +11.3% (+8.2% QoQ) | vs Rs.148.8 cr Q1FY26 / Rs.153.1 cr Q4FY26 |
| Gross profit / margin | Rs.80.4 cr / 48.3% | +16.2% / +210 bps | mix shift to higher-value |
| EBITDA / margin | Rs.29.6 cr / 17.8% | +70 bps YoY / +110 bps QoQ | vs 17.1% Q1FY26 |
| PAT (continuing ops) | Rs.13.9 cr | +14.1% | vs Rs.12.2 cr YoY; flat vs Rs.13.8 cr Q4; PAT margin 8.4% |
| Net worth | Rs.533 cr (31-Mar-26) | vs Rs.466 cr | |
| D/E | 0.45 | ↓ | 0.48 (FY25) → 1.19 (FY24): meaningful 3-yr deleveraging |
| Cash from ops (FY26) | Rs.58.1 cr | — | cash & equiv Rs.37.2 cr (up from Rs.2.6 cr) |
| Receivable days | 131 | ↓ from 145 | target 110-120 |

> **Revenue mix Q1:** Domestic API Rs.92.3 cr (+27% YoY, the growth driver), Exports Rs.50.1 cr, Formulations Rs.23.3 cr — mix expected to "normalize" toward historical as exports recover with easing geopolitics. Balance-sheet dates are FY26 year-end (31-Mar-26), not the June quarter — cross-check next quarter.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth 10-15% for FY27 (and FY28); PAT to grow at a similar rate.**
- **EBITDA margin 18-20%** (FY27-28), improving as peptides/onco/backward-integration lift mix.
- **Capex Rs.40-50 cr/year** (steady-state); no fresh acquisitions planned near-term (digest Gen Rx first).
- **Peptide plant: ~250 kg/yr, commissioning Q4 FY27; first product Semaglutide (India first, plant designed global); revenue from 2028; peak Rs.200-300 cr at 18-20% EBITDA** (ramped over 2-3 yrs).
- **Oncology API facility: target Q4 2028.**
- **Gen Rx (Nashik) commercial production: H2 2027** (post-NCLT/licensing).
- **Cenobamate: FY27 revenue Rs.10-12 cr** (awaiting DCGI NOC + state licence; 8 CDMO marketing tie-ups). **Suvorexant: commercialize next year Q4** (patent-gated).
- **Magnesium L-Threonate: FY27 growth 15-20%; domestic CDMO launch in Q3** (2 brands with partners, ~1-2% of revenue incremental).
- **Vitamin C backward integration (fermentation, with ICT): complete 2029.**
- **CDMO UK/EU (6 CEP approvals): first revenue by FY28-end.**
- **R&D: new 10,000 sq ft Savli facility operational Aug-2026** (100+ scientists); R&D/sales 0.4% (2024) → 2.2% (2026).
- **Long-term: revenue Rs.900-1,000 cr in 2-3 years; export mix to 30-35%** (from ~18-20%).
order book & pipeline (regulatory/produc: Peptides: 6-7 molecules (Semaglutide named; rest confidential). Oncology: Bajaj Oncocare B2C division (launched 2024, 23 states + 3 UTs, 15+ brands; first-in-India Posaconazole 300 mg). CNS: Cenobamate (first-in-India SEC recommendation), Suvorexant (BE done). CDMO exports: DMF filed UK/EU, 6 CEP approvals in last 6-8 months (→ ~1-1.5 yr customer qualification → revenue FY28-end). Institutional supply: Indian Railways, Defence, ESIC, Jan Aushadhi.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **API (foundation):** stable pricing in Q1; domestic API the growth driver (+27%). Backward integration on 8-10 molecules (~20-25% of revenue; +1-2% margin) to cut China dependency. Ascorbic acid & salts (Vitamin C) ~8-10% of revenue — leading domestic maker.
- **Formulations:** shifting to high-margin branded/specialty; Bajaj Oncocare (B2C oncology).
- **Nutraceuticals:** Magnesium L-Threonate (Magtein) — exclusive innovator licence, ~350 MT last year (~10% of revenue), currently export-only to the US patent holder; domestic launch via CDMO partners in Q3.
- **Opium/opiate:** processing opium gum for GoI (toll, not selling opiates); 2 opiate derivative molecules under R&D; seeking bigger GoI allocation.
- **Gen Rx (Nashik):** solid-dosage capacity acquisition, under NCLT; commercial production H2 2027.
- **Discontinued:** Tarapur — 3 loss-making plants for sale; 1 sold, 2 still seeking buyers.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Peptides / GLP-1:** the marquee optionality — Semaglutide first, plant sized for a 4-yr API pipeline; peak Rs.200-300 cr.
- **Specialty CNS formulations:** Cenobamate (first-in-India regulatory milestone) + Suvorexant as CDMO/branded.
- **Backward integration / China+1:** margin + supply-security lever; fermentation-route Vitamin C (patented tech via ICT) a multi-year moat attempt.
- **Nutraceutical (Magtein):** innovator-linked, expanding from export-only to domestic CDMO.
margins & cost dynamics: GM expanded 210 bps to 48.3% on mix; EBITDA 17.8%. Management guides 18-20% EBITDA as peptides/onco/specialty and backward integration (+1-2% on 20-25% of revenue) lift the blend from "high volume/low value" to "low volume/high value." API pricing stable in Q1 (oil/geopolitics-linked). CFO's three finance-function fixes: debt-cost realignment, working-capital allocation, wind-down of discontinued units + plant-level opex optimization.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Capex Rs.40-50 cr/yr. Key milestones to watch for slippage: peptide plant Q4 FY27; oncology API Q4 2028; Gen Rx commercial H2 2027; Savli R&D Aug-2026; Vitamin C fermentation 2029. Inventory was deliberately built up in Q4/Q1 (war-situation buffer for 2 quarters of production) — expected to ease.
capital allocation: Deleveraging is the headline: D/E 1.19 (FY24) → 0.48 (FY25) → 0.45 now; net worth Rs.533 cr. Capex modest (Rs.40-50 cr/yr) and self-funded; no near-term M&A (digest Gen Rx). CFO's 3-yr judge-us metric: **ROE and ROA**. EBITDA→OCF conversion guided to be "materially better" over next 5 yrs vs last 5.
risks & watch-items:
- **Execution/slippage on multiple new plants** (peptide Q4FY27, onco Q4-2028, Gen Rx H2-2027, Vit-C 2029) — revenue back-ended to FY28+; near-term guide is only 10-15%.
- **Working-capital intensity:** inventory holding roughly doubled vs pre-COVID on same revenue (product-count expansion + war buffer); receivables 131 days (high, targeting 110-120) — cash conversion is the credibility test after last year's write-off.
- **Geopolitics/oil** drive API price and export recovery (export mix depressed to ~18-20%).
- **China dependency** in intermediates — backward-integration thesis unproven at scale.
- **Regulatory-gated revenue:** Cenobamate awaiting DCGI/state licence; Suvorexant patent-gated; peptide/CDMO revenues depend on approvals + customer qualification (1-1.5 yr lags).
- First-ever call — no track record of guidance-vs-delivery; one analyst (Sajal) flagged the risk of calls being discontinued in bad times.
management quality / tone: Earnest, accessible, first-call candour — MD Anil Jain gives specific plant dates/capacities/prices (Semaglutide USD 120-150/g); CFO Rohan Parekh direct on finance fixes and the FY-last-year write-off (clarified: one-time, a write-back of income, no cash impact). Some answers vague on quantum (opiate molecules, Suvorexant market size — offered offline). Reasonable transparency for a debut call; consistency across the cycle is the thing to watch.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The reported 17.8% EBITDA is the *pre-transformation* base; the entire equity story is mix-up (peptides/onco/specialty) lifting to 18-20%+ — but the money largely lands FY28+, so FY27 is a bridge year (10-15%).
- Magnesium L-Threonate is a quietly meaningful ~10% of revenue and innovator-linked (supplying the US patent holder) — an under-appreciated nutraceutical annuity now extending to domestic CDMO.
- Deleveraging (D/E 1.19→0.45 in 3 yrs) + first concall + ROE/ROA as the chosen scorecard signals a governance/capital-discipline reset, not a capacity-chasing story.
- Vitamin C via fermentation (no Indian player does this route today; patented tech with ICT) is a genuine import-substitution moat attempt — but 2029, so optional.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
